sentences.text: Fight Club is a 1999 American film based on the 1996 novel of the same name by Chuck Palahniuk .	Fight Club	Fight Club (novel)	Chuck Palahniuk	Chuck Palahniuk	novel of the same name	Fight Club (novel)

The film was directed by David Fincher , and stars Brad Pitt , Edward Norton and Helena Bonham Carter .	David Fincher	David Fincher	Brad Pitt	Brad Pitt	Edward Norton	Edward Norton	Helena Bonham Carter	Helena Bonham Carter
Norton plays the unnamed protagonist , referred to as the narrator , who is discontented with his white-collar job .
He forms a `` fight club '' with soap maker Tyler Durden , played by Pitt , and they are joined by men who also want to fight recreationally .
The narrator becomes embroiled in a relationship with Durden and a dissolute woman , Marla Singer , played by Bonham Carter .

Palahniuk 's novel was optioned by 20th Century Fox producer Laura Ziskin , who hired Jim Uhls to write the film adaptation .	Jim Uhls	Jim Uhls	20th Century Fox	20th Century Fox	optioned	Option (filmmaking)	Laura Ziskin	Laura Ziskin
Fincher was one of four directors the producers considered , and was selected because of his enthusiasm for the film .
Fincher developed the script with Uhls and sought screenwriting advice from the cast and others in the film industry .
The director and the cast compared the film to Rebel Without a Cause -LRB- 1955 -RRB- and The Graduate -LRB- 1967 -RRB- .	Rebel Without a Cause	Rebel Without a Cause	The Graduate	The Graduate
They said its theme was the conflict between a generation of young people and the value system of advertising .	generation of young people	Generation X	value system	value (ethics)#Value system

The director copied the homoerotic overtones from Palahniuk 's novel to make audiences uncomfortable and keep them from anticipating the twist ending .	homoerotic	homoeroticism	twist ending	twist ending
Studio executives did not like the film and restructured Fincher 's intended marketing campaign to try to reduce anticipated losses .

Fight Club failed to meet the studio 's expectations at the box office and initially received polarizing reactions from critics , becoming one of the most controversial and talked-about films of the year .	Fight Club	Fight Club (novel)
Critics praised the acting , directing , themes and messages but debated the explicit violence and moral ambiguity .

Over time , however , reception towards the film has become largely positive with critics and audiences , finding critical and commercial success with its DVD release , which established Fight Club as a cult film .	Fight Club	Fight Club (novel)	cult film	cult film
It is now regarded by many as one of the greatest films of the 1990s .
